clue.text: Perhaps Siamese, but not Thai food, here?

definitions.text: Perhaps Siamese, but not Thai food, here?

parts.words: Perhaps Siamese, but not Thai food, here?
parts.note: Siamese suggests Thailand and its cuisine, but here it is the breed of cat you would meet over coffee in a cafe full of felines

explanation.surface: A diner wonders whether a place serves Siamese cooking, only to find no Thai food on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: Siamese is the old name for things from Thailand, so the eye goes to restaurants; the clue means the cat breed instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue where customers drink coffee among resident felines, so a Siamese might be found there but no Thai dishes.

clue.text: Cup perhaps parted from saucer amicably

indicators.note: the letters are separated out of the run of words saucer amicably, sitting across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A cup and saucer go their separate ways on friendly terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup is one example of pottery ware fired from clay; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Aristo seizes a head of state in rising

indicators.note: the aristocrat grabs hold of the other pieces, so they end up held inside his word

parts.note: a toff is a slang word for an upper-class person, an aristocrat
a king is a monarch heading a state

explanation.surface: A nobleman grabs a ruler during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toff' is British slang for a posh person. 'in' is a link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft lifting from the ground is said to be in the act of leaving the runway, ascending.

clue.text: Rotten way to ride, clear of sides

indicators.note: being clear of something means rid of it, so the word sides is taken off the front of the riding style

parts.note: riding side-saddle, with both legs on one side of the horse, is a way of riding
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poor riding technique that keeps off the flanks of the horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotten' looks like a judgement on the riding but is the definition: an addle egg is a rotten one.
explanation.definitionFit: Addle, as an adjective, describes an egg that has gone bad, putrid and spoilt.

clue.text: Stir up anger about stratagem that finally failed

indicators.note: the word for anger goes around the trimmed stratagem, enclosing it

parts.note: to anger someone is to enrage them

indicators.note: the stratagem's final letter fails to appear, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a coup is a clever, successful stroke or ploy

explanation.surface: Someone whips up fury over a scheme whose end came to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir up' at the head of the clue looks like part of the angry scene, but it is the definition; 'anger' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur someone on or urge them forward, as with spectators cheering a team.

clue.text: Very wonderful edition, which can be folded

parts.note: so is an intensifier meaning very
fab is informal for fabulous, wonderful

explanation.surface: A publisher praises a superb new edition that can be folded up.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch that unfolds into a mattress for guests, so it is furniture which can be folded.

clue.text: Nazi thugs arresting film star

indicators.note: the thugs hold the film captive, so it sits inside their letters

parts.note: the SA, or Sturmabteilung, were the Nazi brownshirt stormtroopers
pic is informal for a picture, a film

explanation.surface: Nazi heavies detain a movie celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' reads as a film star but is the definition on its own: a bright star in Virgo.
explanation.definitionFit: The brightest stellar body in the constellation Virgo bears this name.

clue.text: Putting in every effort, drunk at party

parts.note: full is slang for drunk
a blast is informal for a wild, enjoyable party

explanation.surface: Someone gives it everything, plastered at a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Going at maximum power or volume means holding nothing back, exerting oneself completely.

clue.text: Underwear rebellion?

definitions.meaning: the ... Rebellion was an anti-foreign uprising in China around 1900

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a style of men's shorts and also the Chinese uprising of 1899 to 1901.

clue.text: Decrepit stranger has empty day to fill

indicators.note: the stranger word goes into the gap left in the emptied day, filling it
emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: odder means more strange

explanation.surface: An unfamiliar person must occupy an idle, empty day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranger' reads as a person in the surface but is the comparative of odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaky and feeble with age, the way an old person may totter, frail and infirm.

clue.text: Backed at high price to cover kilometres on a slope

indicators.note: the reversed word covers the kilometre, so that letter goes inside it
backed means turned back, so the word for expensive is read in reverse

parts.note: dear means costly, at a high price
K is short for kilometres

explanation.surface: A gambler wagered expensively on a long-distance race over hilly ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' looks like betting language but reverses DEAR to RAED; 'to cover' puts K inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A raked stage or seating is inclined, tilting at an angle rather than flat.

clue.text: Took a break, having minor illness: sacked!

parts.note: a chill is a mild illness such as a cold
axed means dismissed from a job

explanation.surface: Someone took time off work with a cold, then lost the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang blend of calm down and unwind, meaning someone rested and relaxed for a while.

clue.text: Kicking me out, man unknown: his revenge?

indicators.note: kicking things around sets them in disorder, signalling these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Z is a conventional algebra unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: Someone thrown out by a stranger vows payback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kicking' rearranges MEOUTMAN together with Z (unknown). 'Montezuma's revenge' is slang for traveller's diarrhoea caught in Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztec emperor whose 'revenge' is the jokey name for a stomach upset suffered by visitors to Mexico.

clue.text: At first, railway invested in just sufficient rail

indicators.note: something invested in another is put inside it, so the initial goes into the word for minimal

parts.note: bare means only just enough, as in the bare minimum

indicators.note: only the opening letter of railway is used

explanation.surface: A railway company has put just enough money into new track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rail' looks like more railway talk but means the dancers' handrail.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal handrail fixed to a wall that ballet dancers hold while exercising.

clue.text: Cavern rent by large split

indicators.note: the cavern word is torn open by the letter for large, which sits inside it

parts.note: a cove can mean a cave or sheltered recess in rock
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A cave torn apart by a great crack.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense and participle of cleave, meaning divided or cut apart, as in cloven hoof.

clue.text: Ancient city destination for one dismissed?

parts.note: early means from long ago, ancient
Bath is a Roman spa city in Somerset, England

explanation.surface: An old city is where a sacked person ends up.
explanation.walkthrough: A player sent off in football or rugby is said to be 'sent for an early bath'.
explanation.definitionFit: A player dismissed from a match heads to the changing room to wash ahead of teammates.

clue.text: Unprincipled position spoken in friendship

indicators.note: one word goes inside the other, held within friendship

parts.note: amity means friendly relations
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: An unscrupulous stance is voiced among friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no moral standards at all is a stance that rejects any ethical principle.

clue.text: Fringes dated on ladies' clothing

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sitting on another is placed above it, so it comes first

parts.note: out means out of fashion, dated
skirts are women's garments

explanation.surface: Trimmings on women's garments have gone out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer edges or margins of a town or area, far from its centre.

clue.text: Where Guantanamo's endlessly wrong — it holds a baby

parts.note: Guantanamo Bay is located on the island of Cuba, so it is 'in Cuba'

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter, having no end

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A grim remark about the injustice at Guantanamo, oddly ending with a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated hospital cot that keeps a premature newborn warm and protected.

clue.text: Putting off the calming of excitement?

definitions.meaning: read as de- plus ferment, the removal of agitation or commotion

explanation.definitionFit: Postponement or delay; also, punningly, taking away the ferment, that is the stir or agitation.

clue.text: Daughter spreading powder, a blob on the end of her nose?

definitions.text: a blob on the end of her nose?

indicators.note: powder that is spread gets scattered about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A daughter dabbing on face powder, with a spot left on the tip of her nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A bead of moisture from a dripping nose is jokingly named after the morning droplets on grass.

clue.text: Time after time, winning card one doesn't play

indicators.note: the second time comes after the card, so it follows it

parts.note: an ace is the top card that wins a trick
T again is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A card player wins again and again with a top card.
explanation.walkthrough: TACET is Latin for 'it is silent', marked in a score where an instrument stays quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction telling a player to remain silent for a passage or movement.

clue.text: Torment breaks character — how much can one bear?

indicators.note: the torment word breaks into the character word, sitting inside it

parts.note: tone can mean the general character or feel of something
to nag is to pester or torment

explanation.surface: Persistent torment shatters someone's spirit, leaving them asking how much more they can take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' means carry here: the clue asks a ship's cargo capacity, not a person's endurance.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel's carrying capacity measured in tons, so it says how much the ship can carry.

clue.text: With dry wit, his life's said to be carefree

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the name is heard rather than written

parts.note: the phrase 'the life of Riley' means a carefree, easy existence, so his is Riley

explanation.surface: A deadpan remark that some fellow's life is reputedly easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The life of Riley' is an idiom for a carefree life; 'to be carefree' identifies Riley, and 'said' gives the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking in a mocking, dry, ironic manner is speaking with dry humour.

clue.text: Subverting enemy country

indicators.note: subverting means overturning, so the letters of enemy are turned upside down into a new order

explanation.surface: A hostile power is undermining a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation at the southern tip of the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Criminal broke into cart, a bloomer

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go into the cart word

parts.note: a wain is an old word for a farm wagon or cart

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, signalling the letters of broke are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook smashed into a cart, which was a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bloomer' looks like a mistake but is a flowering plant. 'Criminal' rearranges BROKE to KEROB.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodland plant such as trillium or cuckoo-pint, which flowers, hence a bloomer.

clue.text: American's teeth so much cleaner, they say, given dentist's request?

indicators.note: says how the word is pronounced, specifically in an American accent where the t softens

parts.note: teeth that are cleaner are whiter, and Americans tend to pronounce that word with a soft d sound

explanation.surface: A dentist asks a patient to open up, promising brighter American teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans often pronounce the T in the middle of a word like D, so 'whiter' can sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist asks a patient to open their mouth further, saying more broadly open please.

clue.text: Such furniture needs a bit of care, probably

indicators.note: only a piece of the words care probably is wanted, a stretch running across them

explanation.surface: Furniture of this type will probably require some maintenance.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for reproduction, describing modern copies of antique furniture styles.

clue.text: Violent criminal, a sheep rustler?

definitions.meaning: a thief who smashes a vehicle into a shop front to loot it
taken literally, someone who raids male sheep

explanation.definitionFit: A burglar driving a car through a shop window; read literally, a rustler raiding rams.

clue.text: Precisely correct article about source of rice

parts.note: pat means exactly right, as in having an answer off pat

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the article is read backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A neat definition of an article on where rice comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in India giving its name to a long-grain variety of rice grown in that region.

clue.text: Gasp — that woman not suitable for 1 across

parts.note: to pant is to gasp for breath
her refers to a woman already mentioned

explanation.surface: A woman gasps, judged unfit for the place in 1 across.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 across is a cafe where customers mix with cats; a big wild cat would not do.
explanation.definitionFit: A leopard or other big wild cat would be far too dangerous to keep among cafe customers.

clue.text: Small bottle gets rid of a torment

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes

indicators.note: the word for bottle discards the letter a

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage or nerve

explanation.surface: Someone tips away a little bottle to escape a torment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' is not a container but British slang for nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip or a source of great suffering, an affliction that torments people.
